subject: Post-call: migration checkpoints, compatibility tests, and SDK swap plan
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: migration checkpoints, compatibility tests, and SDK swap plan

Samantha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

1) Goal: validate a low-effort migration path from Finlytics' current hyperscaler-based endpoints to Redwood with minimal prompt diffs and preserved latency/cost profile for batch scoring (50k req/day).

2) Key risks we flagged on the call:
   - Prompt/response subtle differences (tokenization + system prompt handling)
   - SDK/API surface swaps for the ingestion pipeline (Python SDK and one node worker)
   - Latency P95 under peak traffic during overnight batch windows
   - Enterprise compliance evidence (SOC 2 snippets, audit logs retention)

3) Proposed compatibility test plan (week-by-week):
   Week A (this week): sandbox API keys, example prompts and baseline test harness from Finlytics (we'll run local prompt-diff harness).
   Week B: SDK swap smoke (swap the Python client in a canary app; backward-compatible call patterns only).
   Week C: performance sweep (latency/cost matrix at 1k/10k/50k/day patterns).
   Week D: canary rollout with A/B traffic split, quality regression eval (red-team prompts).

4) Ask from you:
   - A canonical prompt set (20–30 prompts covering edge cases), ideally with expected outputs / acceptance criteria.
   - A short list of 2–3 example production traces showing upstream tokenization edge cases (attachments or long system prompts).
   - SOC 2/PII constraints doc (we can sign an NDA if needed).

5) Redwood commitments:
   - We'll provide a prebuilt SDK shim for OpenAI-compatible call patterns so your engineering team only needs to change one import and a small config file.
   - A short script to compute token diffs between outputs and produce per-prompt delta metrics.
   - A one-hour joint runbook workshop the week of Jun 28 to walk through canary steps.

Attached: 20270620-redwood-proposal.pdf (commercial + timeline).

Proposed next call: Tue Jun 22, 10:00–10:30 PT — to review the prompt set and agree on perf targets. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachment: 20270620-redwood-proposal.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@finlytics.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@finlytics.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: migration checkpoints, compatibility tests, and SDK swap plan

Avery — thanks for the succinct recap. This captures what we need. A few clarifications and notes from our side:

- We can provide the canonical prompt set by EOD Thu (a mix of anonymized customer prompts + synthetic edge cases). Will include expected labels for the classification prompts and a few golden responses for NLG examples.
- SOC 2: attached is a redacted snapshot from our cloud provider (note: we'll need Redwood to provide the KMS/HSM integration details for the Private deployment option).
- For the SDK swap: our main constraint is that we cannot change the message format in the ingestion pipeline (we can add headers but cannot alter the JSON body schema). Will the Redwood shim preserve the existing request body fields?

Availability for the call on Tue 22: 10:00 PT works for me and our lead eng will join.

Also, a potential procurement note: if the canary looks clean we may ask for a short-term discounted committed capacity to match current TCO during migration — can you flag who on Redwood's side handles temporary credit/partner discounts so we can loop them in early?

Best,
Samantha Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering | Finlytics
samantha.lopez@finlytics.com

---
Attachment: finlytics-soc2-redacted.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: migration checkpoints, compatibility tests, and SDK swap plan

Samantha — quick technical answers and an initial test checklist below. Happy to review on Tue with your eng team.

1) SDK shim behavior: yes — the shim exposes a drop-in client that mirrors the OpenAI-compatible POST body (messages / prompt / functions) but we can configure the shim to pass through any additional top-level fields unchanged (we won't rewrite your JSON). We'll provide a small adapter with zero-ops pass-through for headers/metadata.

2) Tokenization / prompt diffs: our test harness will compute token-level diffs using both BPE and our internal tokenizer mapping and produce a per-prompt report with: token_count_delta, normalized_logprob_shift, top-3 changed substrings, and a human-readable note when the delta exceeds threshold. Expect an initial report within 48 hours of receiving your prompt set.

3) Performance targets: please confirm P95 target for real-time calls (you mentioned ~280ms today) and nightly batch throughput (50k/day with 2-hour completion window). We will run a p95 sweep and provide a matrix (latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1M-tokens) for three model variants.

4) Compliance / Private deployment: for the Private option we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) and can generate an exportable audit log in the JSONL format you use today. I’ll attach a small snippet of our audit schema in the shared Drive.

Initial checklist we’ll run once we have artifacts from Finlytics:
- Validate prompt set (sanitization + label mapping)
- Run SDK shim smoke on your staging app (sanity + error budget run)
- Trigger 1-hour perf sweep at two concurrency points (can be scheduled with your SRE)
- Run prompt-diff harness and produce CSV + HTML report for review

I’ll bring one of our runtime engineers to Tue's call so we can get into specifics. Thanks for coordinating the procurement contact — Avery will follow up on that.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

Thanks all — putting the calendar invite for Tue 22 10:00 PT now (30 min).

A couple of quick items from commercial/procurement so we don't have surprises:
- Avery, I can handle a short-term committed capacity discount if Finlytics wants a migration credit. I'll need an expected baseline of tokens/month and a target committed months (1–3 months typical).
- Samantha, if you can share the canonical prompt set and the 3 production traces before Thu EOD, Neha's team will run the token-diff report by Fri. If the diffs look small, we can reduce the scope of the canary.
- Also copying our legal contact internally to start a quick standard security addendum — will follow up separately.

See you on the call — Ben
